idiom_name: abstract record + sealed record cases + pattern switch expression
implementation_notes: C# 9 records are the case carriers - positional properties are init-only and the compiler generates value equality, deconstruction, `ToString` and non-destructive `with` - `sealed` on each case stops further derivation, and a `switch` expression with type/property patterns is the eliminator, reporting CS8509 (and CS8524 for unnamed enum values) when an arm is missing; a build can promote those to errors. A record hierarchy is not provably closed, because the generated protected copy constructor lets another assembly derive from it, so the set is closed by convention with a `private` (or `private protected`) constructor on the base plus sealed cases - and even then the compiler still warns unless a discard arm is added, which is why the `closed` class modifier proposal exists. Pre-record code keeps the shape with an abstract class with a private constructor and nested sealed classes, or falls back to an enum plus fields when cases carry no data; keep the classic form for reference-identity cases or interop with mutable class libraries.
pitfalls: Without a discard arm the compiler warns CS8509 because it cannot prove the hierarchy closed; adding `_ => ...` silences the warning and every future missing case with it - the usual compromise is a throwing discard plus WarningsAsErrors for CS8509/CS8524.
Records give init-only properties, not deep immutability: a component holding a `List<T>` or an array stays mutable for every holder unless the constructor copies.
Under nullable reference types a `null` value is not covered by the case arms; the switch needs an explicit `null` arm (or a non-null guarantee) or nulls land in the discard.
`sealed` on the cases alone does not close the set: the protected copy constructor keeps the hierarchy inheritable from other assemblies until the base has a private constructor.
